prompt: What usually results when business operations and procedures are efficient and economical?
choices: More equipment is needed to produce finished products.
Consumer prices are raised in order to increase profits.
Consumers can buy quality products at competitive prices.
Monopolies give all businesses a greater share of the market.
explanation: Consumers can buy quality products at competitive prices. Businesses that are socially responsible focus on ways to improve their operations so that they can meet the needs of consumers while minimizing their own costs. This also maximizes the company's profits so that raising prices may not be necessary. A monopoly exists when a market is controlled by one supplier, and there are no substitute products readily available. An efficient business would produce more products with the equipment it has, rather than having to buy more.

prompt: Which of the following types of computer software programs usually contain a thesaurus:
explanation: Word processing. Most word-processing software programs contain a thesaurus which is a listing of words and their synonyms. This feature enables users to look up alternative words that have the same meaning. The thesaurus helps business employees to prepare accurate written documents and use words that exactly describe or explain the message. Communications programs allow computers to communicate with other computers. Graphics and design software is used to create artwork and drawings rather than text. Presentation software is used to create multimedia presentations.

prompt: Which of the following companies would be principally involved in industrial purchasing:
explanation: Toyota. Industrial purchasing is the process of buying goods and services for internal consumption in the business or for conversion into a final product. Industrial purchasing is the type of purchasing in which manufacturers are principally involved. Safeway, Sears, and Wal-Mart are examples of retail businesses. They are principally involved in buying for resale, or retail buying.

prompt: Which of the following is usually the last step in the buying process:
explanation: Placing the order. Placing the order cannot take place until all the decisions have been made about what to buy, from whom, and for what price. Selecting the method of delivery, deciding on the goods, and negotiat-ing the price are steps in the buying process that occur before an order is placed.

prompt: A characteristic of the accrual method of accounting is that it
choices: records credit purchases when the purchases are made.
is the method most frequently used by small businesses.
is the method used by businesses that don't offer credit.
records transactions at the time the money changes hands.
explanation: Records credit purchases when the purchases are made. The accrual method of accounting records trans-actions at the time they occur even if no money changes hands at that time. This method, therefore, keeps the business up-to-date on the amount of sales rather than on the amount of cash received. The cash accounting method records both income and expenditures at the time the money changes hands. It is the method most frequently used by small businesses, especially those that don't offer credit.

prompt: How long are businesses required to keep their records?
explanation: Varies greatly. The length of time that businesses use and store their records can vary greatly. Some businesses will use certain records indefinitely, while other businesses might maintain information on a seasonal basis or for only one year. The law often determines how long certain records must be maintained.

prompt: The growth of e-commerce is changing the way companies do business by allowing them to
choices: place high prices on their products.
be accessible to customers at all times.
reduce the services they provide customers.
explanation: Be accessible to customers at all times. E-commerce is a business trend that is expanding rapidly because of the Internet and the World Wide Web. E-commerce is changing the way companies do business because it allows them to be accessible to customers at all times. Customers who have access to a computer and the Internet can visit a business's web site and obtain information or shop online at any time of the day or night. As a result, more and more businesses are adding web sites to make their services and products available to customers at all times. The benefit to a business is often increased sales. The growth of e-commerce is increasing competition, which means that businesses often reduce prices and offer additional services to attract customers. Businesses do not use e-commerce to communicate with similar organizations.

prompt: An upscale department store tracks customer purchases made with store credit cards and then tailors promotional messages and merchandise offers to specific clients based on their purchases. What software allows the retailer to manage this strategy?
explanation: Database. Database software allows companies to collect, store, and organize customer information. This information can be used to maintain, analyze, and combine customer information in order to send certain messages to specific customers. Spreadsheet and word-processing software do not perform the functions required by the retailer. Systems tools are used to maintain the computer.

prompt: A business that decides to enlarge its facility and hire additional employees is taking a(n) __________ risk.
explanation: Speculative. Speculative risks are chances of loss that may result in loss, no change, or gain. Deciding to enlarge and hire additional employees is a speculative risk because the business might be successful and increase sales, or it might not be successful and lose sales. The business is speculating that taking the risk will generate gain. Because enlarging a facility and hiring additional employees is a speculative risk, it is not insurable. A liability is a debt that the business owes. Innovative is not a type of business risk.

prompt: A business's balance sheet lists $6,800 in accounts receivable, $13,590 worth of inventory, a building and equipment valued at $245,750, and a mortgage of $150,000. Calculate the business's assets.
explanation: $266,140. A balance sheet is a financial statement that captures the financial condition of the business at a particular moment. One of the three main components of a balance sheet is the business's assets, which include anything of value that the business owns. Assets include items such as cash, accounts receivable, inventory, equipment, buildings, land, and investments. To determine the business's assets, add the accounts receivable, the value of the inventory, and the value of the building and equipment ($6,800 + $13,590 + $245,750 = $266,140). A mortgage is a debt rather than an asset.

prompt: In order to get the full meaning of what someone is saying, you need to listen carefully and to
explanation: Watch the speaker's body language. Body language is gestures, facial expression, posture, and other forms of communicating without words. Our body language often tells more about what we are thinking than the words we say. It is not always possible to know the speaker's background, but it is possible to understand the message without this information. Watching other listeners will prevent you from listening effectively. Making no response will not increase your understanding and may be interpreted by the speaker as a nega-tive reaction.

prompt: Employees should answer the telephone in a businesslike manner in order to
choices: be a candidate for a promotion.
reflect the importance of the job.
handle a lot of calls at one time.
project the image of the business.
explanation: Project the image of the business. The way in which employees handle telephone calls projects the image of the business and its level of service. Handling calls in a businesslike manner can increase business. Using professional telephone techniques includes making the caller feel important, not trying to be important. Being businesslike may enable employees to handle a great many calls or to qualify for promotion, but these are not primary objectives.

prompt: What is the most important component of an effective business letter?
explanation: Message. The message, or body, is the most important component of an effective business letter. The message explains the purpose of the letter and expresses the writer's thoughts to the reader. A business letter is ineffective if the message is not well written and clearly understandable. The opening, address, and heading direct the business letter to the appropriate person.

prompt: An example of a type of simple written report used in marketing is the __________ report.
explanation: Progress. The purpose of a progress report is to give a brief explanation of the status of an activity or project. Business managers often want frequent updates about activities in their departments, and the progress report is intended to provide that information. Research reports and annual reports usually are long, complex reports that provide a great deal of information and often include supplemental materials.

prompt: One of the purposes of staff communication is for managers to provide
choices: employees with access to the grapevine.
explanation: Employees with guidance and direction. Communicating the business's objectives to employees and giving them guidance about doing their work in a manner that will help the firm to achieve those objectives is an important function of effective staff communication. Employees circulate rumors and information among themselves, and this communication is called the grapevine. Staff communication is not addressed to cus-tomers or stockholders.

prompt: In which of the following situations might a business manager be violating the privacy of employees:
choices: Asks job applicants about their qualifications
explanation: Listens to telephone conversations. Most employees consider it a violation of their privacy if managers listen to their telephone conversations. Even in occupations that require constant use of the phone, such as tele-marketing, employees usually expect to be informed when their conversations will be monitored. However, some employers believe they have the right to monitor what employees do on company time. Therefore, workplace privacy is an issue that is still being debated. Employers have the right to ask job applicants about their qualifications and to require pre-employment aptitude tests. These are not considered to be privacy issues. Installing video cameras near registers is a security issue and is done to protect both the business and its employees.

prompt: A large chain often transports shipments of goods from one location to another by using its own
explanation: Trucks. Many large chains, such as Wal-Mart, own fleets of trucks that they use to transport goods from one business site to another. Motorized carriers such as trucks are faster but more expensive to use than rail or water carriers. Even very large businesses do not own rail carriers. Cars are too small for use in transporting goods, and planes are too expensive to use on a regular basis.

prompt: For which of the following markets would producers use a short channel of distribution:
explanation: Local consumers. A short channel can be used when the potential customers are few and/or located close together. The baby boomer, senior citizen, and Generation X markets have many potential customers who are widely dispersed.

prompt: A channel member that knowingly markets a defective product that is determined to be harmful to the environment and then denies responsibility for its actions is taking a(n) _________ approach to social and ethical responsibility.
explanation: Obstructive. An obstructive approach occurs when a business does as little as possible to solve the social or environmental problems it creates when marketing a product. If a business refuses to accept responsibility for actions that harm the environment, the business is being obstructive. When a business takes a defensive approach, it is doing only what is required by law. An accommodating approach is when a business goes beyond its obligation to remedy the situation and extends help to those who ask. In a proactive approach, the business actually seeks out opportunities to contribute to the community/society.

prompt: Calculate the amount due on an invoice for a cruise that costs $789 if the customer pays within 10 days and receives a 5% discount.
explanation: $749.55. Cruise lines frequently offer discounts if customers pay several months in advance. If a travel agent books a cruise for a customer and the customers pays within the specified time, the customer may take the discount. In this example, calculate the amount due on the invoice by first determining the discount ($789 x 5% or .05 = $39.45). Then, subtract the discount from the cost of the cruise to determine the amount due ($789.00 – $39.45 = $749.55).

prompt: How can purchasing agents or buyers benefit from an efficient receiving process?
choices: They are able to read price stickers to determine a product's weight and price.
They can find out what goods are on back order and when they will be delivered.
They learn the appropriate way to handle fragile goods when they arrive at the business.
They enjoy easy access to the receiving area since its doors are open throughout the day.
explanation: They can find out what goods are on back order and when they will be delivered. An efficient receiving process supports the sales effort by keeping track of the availability of goods. Receiving workers can keep buyers up-to-date on the status of shipments so that the buyers know what goods have been delivered, what goods are being shipped, and what goods are on back order. If a part of a shipment is on back order, the buyer may ask receiving to find out from the vendor when the back-ordered goods will be delivered. Buyers do not handle goods when the goods arrive at the business. Customers read price stickers to determine a product's weight and price. Buyers should not be able to access the receiving area easily—doors to the receiving area should be kept locked to limit theft and pilferage.

prompt: What shipping method would a business probably use to ship a small order to a customer in the next province?
explanation: Motor carrier. The majority of small shipments that are transported over short distances are shipped by motor carrier; therefore, a business shipping a small order to a customer in the next province probably would send it by truck. The trucking industry handles a large percentage of shipping and is fast and flexible because trucks can deliver to the customer's door. Motor carriers also are used to supplement railroad, commercial airline, and waterway shipping because those transportation methods cannot deliver directly to a customer's door. Railroads are often used to ship heavy items. Commercial airlines are expensive and often used to ship emergency or perishable items. Waterways are generally used to ship bulk freight such as coal or grain.

prompt: Which of the following products would need to be protected from the weather during storage but would not need special care or services:
explanation: Pencils. A product, such as pencils, that only needs to be protected from rain or snow can be stored in a general merchandise warehouse. Bricks are stored outside since they would not be damaged by weather. Cotton is stored in a special storage facility designed for farm products. Oranges need to be stored and transported in a refrigerated environment due to their perishability.

prompt: What type of channel conflict might occur if the manufacturer of a specific brand begins to allow retailers other than the authorized retailers to sell the brand-name products?
explanation: Vertical. Vertical conflict occurs among different levels of the same channel of distribution, such as between a manufacturer and its authorized retailers. If a manufacturer begins to allow retailers other than those cur-rently authorized to sell the brand-name products, the retailers may become upset because others now have the same products. Expanding the number of outlets for the products may be good for the manufacturer but detrimental to the retailers because they will have more competition. Horizontal conflict occurs among busi-nesses at the same channel level, such as between the authorized businesses in the same city. Contractual and industrial are not types of channel conflict.

prompt: Cashregister tapes and shipping forms used by a business would be classified as industrial
explanation: Supplies. Supplies are products that are constantly being purchased and used up in the operation of a business. Parts are items that will become part of a final product without additional processing. Materials become part of a finished product after they have been processed. Equipment is industrial products used in the operation of a business but not in the actual production of a good or service.

prompt: Excess demand and excess supply cause changes in
explanation: Market price. Market price is the actual price that prevails in a market at any particular moment. Excess demand and excess supply cause fluctuations in market price. The relative price ratio is the relationship between two prices as compared to each other. The price index compares today's prices with those of previous years. Price determination is the process of setting prices.

prompt: The routine costs involved in running a business are referred to as
explanation: Operating expenses. Business expenses are divided into two general categories: operating expenses and cost of goods. Operating expenses are expenditures necessary to keep the business running. Some typical operating expenses include payroll, rent, insurance, and utility bills. Cost of goods is the amount of money a business pays for the products it sells. Cash flow is the movement of money into and out of the business. Cumulative costs would be costs that were accumulated over a period of time.

prompt: Which of the following is a standard used in measuring an individual worker's productivity:
explanation: Time. A worker's productivity can be measured by the time it takes to complete a particular task or job, the amount of work produced, or the monetary value of the work. For example, a salesperson who can make a sale in half the time of another salesperson is said to be twice as productive. Inputs are those resources used in producing goods or services. The method used may increase or decrease productivity, but it is not a standard of measurement. A ratio is a mathematical expression of the comparison between two factors.

prompt: GDP figures for Canada include the value of
choices: goods that are not sold in the marketplace.
goods that Canada produces in other countries.
transactions for which no receipts are kept.
all production for which money is exchanged.
explanation: All production for which money is exchanged. Gross domestic product (GDP) is the final total value of all the goods produced within a country's geographic boundaries within a certain time period. It includes the pro-duction of both goods and services for which money is exchanged. Goods that are not sold in the market-place and transactions for which no receipts are kept are not included. Goods that Canada produces in other countries would be part of the GDP for those countries.

prompt: The buying and selling of goods and services between nations is called
explanation: International trade. Since nations have unequal distributions of economic resources, they must depend upon each other for the goods and services they need and cannot produce themselves. Protectionism is a govern-ment's policy to protect domestic industries and businesses against foreign competition. The buying and selling of products within a country is domestic trade. Imports are the goods and services bought from other nations.

prompt: A business that obtains financing in order to stock more inventory is often able to
explanation: Increase sales. Sales often increase when businesses have more inventory available for customers. Financing helps businesses to obtain the funds they need to buy more inventory. The availability of financing provides more inventory, which often leads to increased sales and a more profitable business. Businesses that obtain financing in order to stock more inventory do not decrease loans, increase wages, or decrease risks.

prompt: Mr. and Mrs. Smith are planning to purchase a new, 24-foot, camper trailer. Which of the following types of credit would be best for the Smiths if they now have less than half the purchase price:
explanation: Installment credit. Installment credit is a type of credit account set up to handle one total amount of credit that is to be paid off in regular installments. It is commonly used to purchase large, expensive items. Revolving credit is a type of credit account that limits the total amount of money that may be owed and charges interest on outstanding balances. Open or regular credit allows credit users to buy at any time during a set period, usually 30 days.

prompt: Which of the following is one way that businesses use marketing information:
explanation: To predict change. Businesses need a wide variety of information in order to make decisions about how the business will market its goods or services. Businesses gather marketing information about their customers, the competition, the economy, and sales trends in order to predict what may occur in the future. The use of marketing information allows businesses to prepare for change and adapt in order to remain successful. Businesses often develop surveys and conduct research to obtain the marketing data they need to analyze in order to predict change.

prompt: Which function of a marketing-information management system involves changing the form of marketing information to make it more useful?
explanation: Information processing. Sometimes marketing data are not useful in their raw form. Their format must be processed or changed to be more effective. Information reporting is concerned with the movement of data to the appropriate parties. Information gathering deals with the collection of data, while marketing research deals with gathering information to solve a specific problem.

prompt: Which of the following is information about customers that businesses often monitor in order to make marketing decisions:
explanation: Buying behavior. Buying behavior is the usual purchasing methods of consumers; it is the process they use to decide what they will buy and from whom they will buy. By monitoring consumers' buying behavior, busi-nesses are able to find out what type of products they buy, how much they spend on the products, and what businesses they buy from on a regular basis. Businesses can use this information to make marketing deci-sions such as whether to offer lower prices in order to take customers away from competitors. Businesses usually are not able to obtain information about a customer's personal character. Businesses usually need consumers' permission before obtaining information about their credit rating. Supplemental income is income from sources other than a primary job and often is private information that is not available to businesses.

prompt: Sources of marketing data that are outside the business are called __________ information sources.
explanation: External. External information sources are located outside the business. Internal information sources are located inside the business. Internal sources are more likely to be private than external sources. Either source could provide information that has been published.

prompt: Which of the following research methods might a business use that is inexpensive, reaches a large number of people, and obtains information about its customers' needs:
explanation: Direct-mail surveys. The mailed survey is an inexpensive way to reach a large group of customers or poten-tial customers. Surveys usually contain a variety of questions that will help a business obtain information about its customers' needs. Telephone surveys, focus groups, and personal interviews are more costly, take longer to implement, and do not reach as large of an audience as mailed surveys.

prompt: How does marketing research help a business to implement the marketing concept?
choices: By setting goals for the business
By identifying consumers' wants and needs
explanation: By identifying consumers' wants and needs. The marketing concept is a philosophy of conducting business that is based on the belief that all business activities should be aimed toward satisfying consumer wants and needs while achieving company goals. Marketing research helps the business to implement the marketing concept by providing it with information about what consumers want, need, and are likely to buy. Marketing research cannot solve a business's problems or prevent financial losses. The business sets its own goals which may or may not be based on marketing-research information.

prompt: What do businesses often do with the marketing information they collect from consumer questionnaires?
choices: Enter it into a computer for analysis
Assign a numeric value to the responses
Arrange the names in alphabetical order
Organize it according to the date received
explanation: Enter it into a computer for analysis. After a business collects marketing information from consumer ques-tionnaires, it processes the information to make it useful. Many businesses enter the data into a computer that is able to tabulate, evaluate, or analyze the information according to specific criteria. Simply gathering information from questionnaires will not be helpful unless the business analyzes it to determine what it means and how it can be used. A business assigns a numeric value to the responses in a questionnaire before distributing the questionnaire to consumers. Businesses usually do not organize the information according to the date received, or arrange in alphabetical order the names of consumers who complete the questionnaire.

prompt: One of the reasons why a chain of supermarkets might analyze and interpret the marketing information contained in databases is to
explanation: Compare variables. A chain of supermarkets might analyze and interpret the marketing information con-tained in databases in order to compare several variables that change from store to store. For example, one supermarket might be located in an affluent community while another one is located in an inner-city neigh-borhood. The chain might analyze the information in its database concerning both communities in order to make appropriate marketing decisions such as the type of goods to offer in each location. Although the chain provides the same type of goods and services to both communities, it needs to analyze data in order to know if the consumers in each community have different wants and needs. Before analyzing databases to compare variables, a chain of supermarkets might survey customers and tabulate the findings. A chain would not analyze databases in order to organize products.

prompt: What are the primary advantages of using descriptive statistics?
choices: You can reach conclusions that extend beyond what the data shows.
It allows you to summarize data and make comparisons across units.
You are able to make charts easily and create unbound reports faster.
The data is not described in numerical form and can be transferred easily.
explanation: It allows you to summarize data and make comparisons across units. Descriptive statistics are summaries of data that make large amounts of information more manageable. Reaching conclusions involves making inferences rather than using descriptive statistics. Descriptive statistics can be described in numerical form. The use of descriptive statistics does not necessarily enable you to make charts easily.

prompt: Which of the following is an important reason why the findings of a business's marketing study should be effectively communicated to the business's managers:
explanation: To make the information useful. Presenting the findings of a business's research project, either orally or in writing, is important because the information is not useful until it is effectively communicated to the people who make the decisions. The managers need to know the results of the marketing study and often rely on others to develop oral presentations or written reports that will explain the findings in a clear and concise manner and provide them with the accurate information they need to make good marketing decisions. The process of presenting the findings of the marketing study might include explaining the research methods and summarizing the research goals. The findings of a marketing study are not communicated to managers in order to review the presentation style.

prompt: Which of the following is part of the promotional element of marketing:
explanation: Advertising. The promotion element of marketing refers to the various types of communication that mar-keters use to communicate information about goods, services, images, and/or ideas to achieve a desired outcome. The most commonly used promotional elements are sales promotion, advertising, personal selling, and publicity. Discounts and credit are part of the price element. Packaging is part of the product element.

prompt: Which of the following is an example of a consumer market:
choices: Music lover at a free concert
explanation: Music lover buying CDs. A music lover buying CDs qualifies as a market because s/he has an unfulfilled desire and the financial resources to satisfy it. A consumer market is a customer or potential customer who purchases goods or services to satisfy personal desires. A customer must have the financial resources, a need or desire for the product, and the willingness to pay for it in order to be considered a market. The other alternatives lack these characteristics.

prompt: Which of the following would most likely indicate that an adjustment in a sales forecast is needed:
choices: The anticipated economic recovery did not occur.
The company's target markets will remain the same.
Promotional strategies will remain the same for next year.
explanation: The anticipated economic recovery did not occur. This would indicate that the current sales forecast is probably off target since it would have been based on the anticipated recovery. Sales forecasts should be prepared according to the needs of the business based on how much the firm sold in the previous year. They should be adjusted as necessary for any changes in the firm's marketing plan or in the economy. The other alternatives are aspects of a marketing plan that appear to be stable.

prompt: Which of the following is a benefit to the business of effective human relations:
explanation: Increased productivity. Productivity is the amount and the value of goods and services produced (outputs) from set amounts of resources (inputs). Effective human relations in the workplace improves employee morale which in turn increases the amount of work employees accomplish. Effective human relations also increases customer loyalty and reduces absenteeism.

prompt: Employees who always keep their commitments to customers are building positive relationships with those customers by being
explanation: Dependable. Employees who are dependable do what they say they will do and keep their commitments to customers. When employees offer to do something for customers, they must live up to the terms of the commitment in order to build positive relationships. Customers appreciate dependable employees and often return to a specific business because of them. Assertive employees stand up for their rights. Sociable employees are friendly. Creative employees develop unique ideas and solutions to problems. These are good characteristics for employees to have, but they do not involve keeping commitments.

prompt: When confused by things that they do not fully understand, assertive individuals are likely to
choices: change the subject to something familiar.
cover up their confusion with conversation.
ask questions to clarify their understanding.
explanation: Ask questions to clarify their understanding. Assertive people are not embarrassed by their confusion about things they do not fully understand. They ask questions in order to improve their understanding. Pretending to understand, talking to cover confusion, and changing the subject are all negative responses to the situa-tion that benefit no one.

prompt: "I like this sofa, but I just don't know whether my family will like it," is a statement characteristic of a __________ customer.
explanation: Slow/Methodical. Slow/Methodical customers require a lot of time to make a purchase because of shyness or difficulty in making a choice or buying decision. These customers may lack confidence in their ability to make the correct choice. Disagreeable customers are unpleasant and hard to help. Domineering/Superior customers are overly confident and feel they know more and are better than the average person. Suspicious customers question everything and want facts and proof before being convinced that something is true.

prompt: The first step in dealing with a customer who has a complaint is to
choices: explain why the customer is wrong.
let the customer explain the problem.
explanation: Let the customer explain the problem. A complaint is an expression of dissatisfaction about a good, service, or policy. Customers who have complaints should have a chance to explain the problem without interruption. If the complaint is handled poorly, the customer may never return; but handling complaints effectively can build goodwill. The customer's comments should not be ignored, and the customer should not be made to feel that s/he is in the wrong. Handling complaints is the salesperson's responsibility, and a manager would only be called in as a last resort.

prompt: Which of the following is a benefit of orienting new employees:
explanation: Reduces anxiety about the job. Orienting new employees answers many of their questions about the job and the business. This helps to reduce any anxiety the employees may have about a new environment. Orienta-tion sessions may or may not be formal. A good orientation program generally reduces the need for training. Introducing new employees to current staff should be part of orientation but does not necessarily help them to make friends.

prompt: Which of the following is a way that a business can use the money it saves by controlling expenses:
explanation: Expansion. In order for a business to grow and expand, it needs to earn more money than it spends. One way of obtaining additional funds is to control expenses. A business that successfully controls its expenses and earns a profit can invest that money in growing and expanding the business. Evaluation is the process of appraising or judging. Consolidation is the joining of two or more companies to form a new company. Orientation is job preparation or induction training for new employees.

prompt: Why does being interested and enthusiastic help people to attract friends?
choices: People prefer being with interested, enthusiastic people rather than with boring, indifferent people.
People prefer being with people who are focused on their work rather than with people who take extended breaks.
People prefer spending time with people who discuss sports rather than people who talk about work.
People prefer spending time with people who need help rather than with people who can function independently.
explanation: People prefer being with interested, enthusiastic people rather than with boring, indifferent people. Regard-less of the topic, it is more fun and enjoyable to associate with interested, enthusiastic individuals rather than boring, indifferent people. Being focused on work or being in need of help might reduce a person's ability to be interested and enthusiastic.

prompt: Assuming that all people of a certain nationality will work long hours for low pay is an example of
explanation: Stereotyping. A stereotype is a set image or an assumption about a person, a group of people, or a thing. Assuming that all people of a certain nationality will work long hours for low pay is stereotyping because it makes a judgment about a group as a whole rather than about individuals. Discrimination is unfair treatment of a person or a group based on the person's or group's characteristics. Prejudice is opinion or judgment that is based on feeling or hearsay, rather than fact. Harassment is any kind of behavior toward another person that is carried out for the purpose of annoying or threatening the individual.

prompt: Organized people define their priorities in order to make sure that they
explanation: Get important jobs done first. Organized people routinely look at the things they need to accomplish in order to make sure they do the most important ones first. This may result in getting a lot done, but that is not the purpose of setting priorities. There are no specific rules about defining priorities, and it does not increase self-esteem.

prompt: Several employees are facing the possibility of being laid off from work. By concluding that they should look for new jobs before that happens, they are
explanation: Solving problems. Problem solving is the process of deciding how to handle and solve a problem. All prob-lem solving involves making decisions because there are many solutions to problems. Individuals always go through the decision-making process to choose one of the alternatives that they think will solve the problem. By deciding to look for new jobs, the employees are solving their problem. The employees are not gathering information, doing research, or asking questions.

prompt: Which of the following would not be scheduled on a daily "To Do" list:
choices: Activities that must be done next month
Required activities from the master list
New activities that must be completed the next day
Activities that were previously scheduled for the day
explanation: Activities that must be done next month. A daily "To Do" list contains the activities that a person plans to accomplish the next day rather than in the next month. This list should be prepared at the end of one day for the next day and should be based on the activities that appear on a weekly master list, activities that were previously scheduled for the upcoming day, and new activities that have surfaced during the day and must be completed the next day.

prompt: What marketing career involves determining why customers do what they do?
explanation: Marketing research. A marketing researcher could be classified as the "Sherlock Holmes" of marketing. These investigators look for clues as to what customers want and need, as well as why customers do what they do. Careers in distribution/warehousing physically link products with consumers by delivering them to customers when they are needed. Careers in advertising involve catching customer attention and informing customers about products, companies, and/or ideas. Sales careers involve satisfying customer needs with products.

prompt: Which of the following is a guideline to follow in writing a follow-up letter after a job interview:
choices: Make the letter chatty and personal.
Review your job skills in detail.
explanation: Be brief, concise, and prompt. A follow-up letter after a job interview should be businesslike, not chatty and personal. It should be written on plain stationery of a subdued color, not on colorful notepaper. It should also be very short, to the point, sent promptly after the interview, and appreciative of the time the interviewer gave you.

prompt: Manuel is preparing his job résumé, but he has never held a paying job. He has only worked for his father and done some volunteer work in the community. What should Manuel do about the work-experience section of his job résumé?
choices: He should not include a work-experience section.
He should explain that he hasn't had a real job.
He should list his family job and volunteer work.
He should describe the kind of job he'd like to have.
explanation: He should list his family job and volunteer work. Listing the work he has done for his father and his volunteer work will show the interviewer that Manuel is accustomed to carrying out certain responsibilities. This is a better choice than leaving out a section on work experience. The kind of job the individual would like to have would be included in the objectives section of the résumé. It would not be necessary, or appropriate, to explain that he hasn't had a real job, as the interviewer will see that at a glance.

prompt: What should employees in today's changing world do to prevent their skills from becoming obsolete?
explanation: Continue their education. Employees need to continue learning and improving their skills in order to keep up with changes in technology. For example, many businesses are replacing existing equipment with advanced models that are more complex or perform more operations. Employees need to be willing to learn the skills necessary to operate advanced equipment because their former skills are obsolete. Employees should not change jobs frequently. Modifying personal behavior will not necessarily prevent employees' skills from be-coming obsolete unless they also continue their education. Many employees are responsible for performing specific tasks and are not able to delegate that responsibility to others.

prompt: A group of people in the same industry or geographic area who join forces to search for solutions to common problems is called
explanation: A trade association. Trade associations have been formed on local, state, and national levels; and increased profit for association members is usually the group's primary goal. The chamber of commerce, also known as a business federation, is an organization that encourages twoway communication between consumers and the business community. A civic organization is a service club such as the Lions Club.

prompt: Which of the following is an example of price in the financial services industry:
explanation: Interest on a loan. Prices are attached to anything of value for which consumers are willing to make a money exchange. When a customer obtains a loan from a financial institution, the customer repays the loan with interest. The interest is the price the customer pays to the bank for the purchase of the loan. A debit to an account occurs when a customer writes a check or withdraws funds from an account and does not neces-sarily involve a fee to the bank. The balance on a loan is the amount remaining to be repaid. A credit to an account involves depositing funds to an account.

prompt: Charging premium prices for lumber to hurricane victims because supply is limited is
explanation: Unethical and legal. Shortages of supply when demand is high often generates high prices. Most countries have laws forbidding price gouging for lifesaving products after a tragedy. The laws do not extend to products that are not lifesaving, even if they are in great demand and have no substitutes. Lumber is not a lifesaving product; therefore, it is legal to charge premium prices. However, it is unethical to do so because a supplier is making a huge profit as a result of another person's tragedy.

prompt: Businesses that come under government control often set a target return of profit because they
choices: need to earn very high profits.
must abide by unfair trade practices.
are not allowed to earn a reasonable profit.
may be investigated if they earn high profits.
explanation: May be investigated if they earn high profits. The government allows businesses under its control to earn enough profit to pay dividends to their stockholders and have some capital left to invest in the business. If the businesses earn too much profit, the government may investigate to see whether consumers are being overcharged. These businesses must avoid any unfair trade practices—business activities that are not fair to consumers or to other businesses.

prompt: At which stage of a product's life cycle does commercialization occur?
explanation: Introductory. The introductory stage occurs when the product first appears in the marketplace. Commercial-ization is the point in the introductory stage at which a product goes into full-scale production, the marketing plan is put into place, service and sales training are done, and the product's life cycle begins. Growth, maturity, and decline are life-cycle stages that follow the introductory stage.

prompt: One of the ways in which a business can revive a product that is in the decline stage of the product life cycle is to __________ the product.
explanation: Repackage. Repackaging the product can help it to catch the attention of additional customers and thus prolong its life cycle. The product cannot be positioned since that has already been done. However, it could be repositioned to prolong its life. Removing or discontinuing the product would end the product life cycle, rather than reviving the product.

prompt: Specifying criteria for products so that they will be the same quality is the process of establishing
explanation: Standards. Standards are statements that specify a product's size, contents, and/or quality. Standards help businesses and consumers by providing a "yardstick" by which products can be measured. Deviation occurs when a product does not meet standards. Competition is the rivalry between two or more businesses to attract scarce customer dollars. Transportation is the physical movement of a product through the channels of distribution.

prompt: In product/service management, a major disadvantage of rapid technological changes is the
choices: number of new products entering the market.
rate at which existing products become obsolete.
increase in customer satisfaction and profitability.
explanation: Rate at which existing products become obsolete. Technology advances so rapidly that products introduced to market are quickly being reintroduced with upgrades or changes that make the original obsolete. The problem is that many technically advanced products have a short life cycle because more advanced products take their place. Increasing the introduction of new products and improving customer awareness will increase customer satisfaction and, as a result, increase sales and profitability. These are advantages of new technology.

prompt: A specialty business whose target market is the career woman with expensive taste would have a product mix with __________ assortment.
explanation: Narrow variety, deep. The terms used to describe the scope of a business's product mix include broad or narrow and shallow or deep. A product mix with narrow variety refers to a limited number of product lines. A deep assortment refers to a great many items in each product line. This business offers a great many items of clothing and accessories but only in a few product lines. A broad product mix offers many product lines. A shallow mix offers few items in the product line.

prompt: Businesses benefit from repeat sales to consumers who have brand
explanation: Loyalty. When consumers get into the habit of buying certain brands, known as brand loyalty, they auto-matically make repeat purchases of that brand. This reduces the amount of time needed to make a sale. Experience with a brand does not always generate sales. Consumers who have developed resistance to a brand or object to it for some reason are not likely to buy it repeatedly.

prompt: In the communication process, why is it important for the sender to effectively encode the message to be sent?
choices: To leave the message open to interpretation
To obtain valuable feedback from the receiver
To ensure that the receiver will understand it
To make it easier for the sender to communicate
explanation: To ensure that the receiver will understand it. Encoding a message involves choosing words, symbols, or signs that will be understood by the receiver. Unless a message is encoded effectively, it will not be under-stood or interpreted correctly by the receiver. Encoding does not make a message easier to communicate. Messages should be clear and not open to interpretation. Obtaining valuable feedback occurs after the receiver has received the message.

prompt: The promotion of baseballnut ice cream during baseball season would be classified as __________ promotion.
explanation: Product. Product promotion is a type of promotion that aims to persuade customers to buy a specific good or service. Public-service promotions inform consumers about noncontroversial issues that are in the public's best interest. Patronage promotion is designed to promote a firm's features or prestige. Institutional promo-tion is used to create a certain image or reputation.

prompt: Which of the following is not a form of promotion:
explanation: Branding. Branding is the ongoing decision-making process about the use of brands. The brand will prob-ably be used in promotions, but branding the product is not a form of promotion. Personal selling is the form of promotion that uses planned, personalized communication in order to influence purchase decisions and to ensure satisfaction. Coupons and visual merchandising are examples of sales promotion, promotional activ-ities other than advertising, personal selling, and publicity that stimulate consumer purchases.

prompt: Which of the following is an example of a socially responsible promotion:
explanation: Supporting worthwhile causes. Social responsibility is the duty of business to contribute to the well-being of society. One way that businesses exhibit social responsibility is by developing promotions that support worthwhile causes. Some businesses advertise in support of charitable organizations or sponsor ad cam-paigns to encourage young people to stay in school. They may focus on helping the public to understand important health issues or safety concerns. Promotions that announce upcoming sales, explain business policies, or describe recent renovations are not examples of socially responsible promotions.

prompt: What type of promotional media might a business use to target a specific audience of customers at home?
explanation: Direct mail. Direct mail is a promotional medium that comes to consumers' homes in the form of letters, catalogs, postcards, and folders. Of the media listed, direct mail is the only one in which the business can control who will receive the promotional message. Television and magazines are available to a broad, general audience. Billboards are a type of out-of-home media.

prompt: Which of the following is bad advice for someone writing advertising copy:
choices: Coordinate copy with other ad elements
Find out in which media the ad will appear
explanation: Disregard competitors' advertisements. By studying the advertisements of competitors, copywriters can learn which techniques are used and which features or benefits are emphasized. Other valuable information helpful to copywriters includes knowledge of the media, other ad elements with which the copy should be coordinated with, and the promotional objectives of the business.

prompt: One of the advantages of using databases in advertising is that it allows businesses to
explanation: Segment customers. A database is a computerized collection of information. Many businesses collect a wide variety of information about customers, such as age and location, and maintain this information in a database. Then, businesses can manipulate the data in order to segment customers into specific categories, such as senior citizens, people who live in Florida, or people who earn more than $50,000 a year. Busi-nesses can develop advertising that is directed to the segments that are most likely to buy rather than to all potential customers. The use of databases makes the advertising more effective and less expensive be-cause it targets specific segments of the market. Businesses do not use databases in advertising to identify trends, target suppliers, or analyze forecasts.

prompt: Which of the following often triggers an advertiser's banner ad to appear on a search engine's web page:
explanation: Specific word. Some search engines offer advertisers the option of having their banner ads pop up each time a viewer searches for a specific word. For example, an ad for a sporting goods store might appear every time a viewer searches for the word "basketball." Search engines usually charge a flat monthly fee for this type of advertising. A clickthrough occurs each time a visitor to a web site clicks on an advertisement and is automatically transported to the advertiser's web page. The impression rate is the number of times the advertisement is viewed. A transaction is a business activity such as a sale or a purchase.

prompt: Most news releases are written in an "inverted pyramid" style, which means that
choices: all the vital information is presented first.
the news release does not have to have a lead.
the news release is not likely to be cut by the media.
each succeeding paragraph is more important than the last.
explanation: All the vital information is presented first. In the inverted pyramid style, which is the style in which newspaper stories are written, all of the vital information is presented in the first paragraph. The opening sentence of the paragraph is called the lead because it leads into the main part of the story. The result of using this style is that each succeeding paragraph is less important than the one preceding it. This means that if the media cut the story in order to fit the available space, they can cut from the end of the story without leaving out any vital information.

prompt: Which of the following promotional activities should be coordinated with a business's advertising:
explanation: Special events. Special events are promotional activities that may include a wide variety of activities such as lectures, demonstrations, and celebrity appearances. A business should coordinate its advertising and special events in order to obtain the maximum results. The advertising will inform customers of the special events, and once these customers have been drawn into the business, the sales staff will have the oppor-tunity to encourage them to buy. Market trips involve the buyers for a business visiting a certain market in order to purchase products for resale. Trade shows are exhibitions at which manufacturers and suppliers in a particular industry display their goods. Customer services are activities, such as free delivery and gift wrapping, that increase customer satisfaction and create goodwill.

prompt: Customers are more likely to trust businesses and products when the salesperson is
explanation: Self-confident. The salesperson's confidence gives customers confidence in the business. They feel that the company will stand by its promises and that they have made a good buying decision. Customers often do not respond well to salespeople who are aggressive, talkative, or insistent.

prompt: Who should take full responsibility for any misunderstandings that are part of a sales transaction?
explanation: Salesperson. When a misunderstanding occurs, it is important for the salesperson to deal with the situation tactfully. Regardless of who is at fault, the salesperson should take complete responsibility for the problem. The customer must be made to feel that the problem is being taken care of promptly and competently. The customer should not take responsibility for the problem. The supervisor and the manager should become involved only if the salesperson is not able to remedy the problem.

prompt: In order to prepare a feature-benefit chart, a salesperson must know
choices: the number of products in stock.
the name of the product's distributor.
explanation: Facts about the product. A feature-benefit chart lists product features and their corresponding benefits. The number of products in stock has no relation to a feature-benefit chart. Facts about customers and the name of the product's distributor are not used in a feature-benefit chart.

prompt: What is often an effective technique for a salesperson to use when selling goods and services to groups?
explanation: Encourage interaction. Selling to groups is often more difficult than selling to one person because of the number of people involved in making the buying decision. One way for a salesperson to effectively sell to a group is to encourage interaction among the members of the group. The salesperson can encourage inter-action by opening up the discussion and giving each member an opportunity to participate. A salesperson should be tolerant of all points of view and keep dominant members from taking control of the conversation. A salesperson should follow an agenda and focus on a few main topics. It is not realistic to try to question each participant in the group. Frequent summaries help the group to draw conclusions and move on to the next point.

prompt: Which of the following would be most likely to make an informative presentation to employees about the specific features and benefits of a new line of products they will be selling:
explanation: The firm's buyer. Before purchasing a new line of products for the business, buyers investigate the line thoroughly. They would have a personal interest in providing salespeople with selling information because they want the new line to be launched successfully. The head of the firm would not be likely to have specific selling information about a product line. The lead salesperson would probably not have the knowledge needed since this is a new product line. The human resources director is involved in the selection and hiring of employees.

prompt: One factor leading to differences in the ways salespeople use the selling process is the
explanation: Nature of the product. Factors leading to differences in the use of the selling process include the nature of the product. Large, expensive items may require more time and effort to sell. Tangible items that customers can see and handle may be easier to sell than intangible items. The mood of the salesperson, the season of the year, and the availability of credit are not factors affecting differences in the use of the selling process.

prompt: Katherine is very interested in fashion and always buys the newest styles, regardless of the price. Which of the following personality types is Katherine demonstrating:
explanation: Informed. The informed personality is characterized by showing confidence in choices, spending for quality, being a trendsetter, and/or wanting the best. Katherine is demonstrating the informed personality by buying the newest styles and making a purchase, no matter what the price is. The impulsive personality is charac-terized by the customer asking few questions, selecting items quickly, and/or shopping leisurely. The decisive personality is characterized by the customer asking for specific merchandise, acting in a direct manner, and/or knowing what s/he wants. The difficult personality is characterized by the customer being disagreeable, suspicious, slow, or domineering.

prompt: Identify the factor affecting needs and wants in the following situation: For his birthday, Jonathan wanted a tricycle, coloring books, and toy soldiers.
explanation: Jonathan's age level. Jonathan's desire for a tricycle, coloring books, and toy soldiers is directly related to his age. As he grows older, his wants and needs will change. Jonathan's place of residence, current economic conditions, and the time of year are not related to this situation.

prompt: Which of the following is an example of assisting customers in making buying decisions:
choices: Using general terms to explain features
explanation: Demonstrating product knowledge. Demonstrating product knowledge is vital in the assistance of customers. Hesitation or questions left unanswered by the salesperson may prevent the customer from reaching one or more of the five buying decisions. Salespeople should know their goods and services in order to help customers reach product decisions. Salespeople should not be forceful or show indifference when assisting customers. Salespeople should avoid using general terms.

prompt: Which of the following is a customer benefit of the salesperson's use of probing:
explanation: It reduces product dissatisfaction. Throughout the presentation, salespeople should use probes in order to determine the customer's needs. This helps the salesperson to suggest products that are most likely to meet those needs and, therefore, be satisfactory to the customer. Uncovering hidden objections is a benefit to the salesperson because it reveals the real reasons customers don't buy. Probing can speed up the sale and may enhance the firm's image, which are benefits to the salesperson and/or the business.

prompt: Most businesses have times when stock of a particular item is in short supply. If this occurs, the salesperson should utilize
explanation: Product substitution. Product substitution involves suggesting an item other than the one requested when that item is out of stock or when the salesperson recognizes the customer's true needs. Tradingup is selling higher priced items than originally requested by the customer. Nonpersonal selling does not involve contact with customers. Suggestion selling attempts to increase the customer's purchase by suggesting additional items after the original decision to buy has been made.

prompt: A salesperson explains to the business that the energy saver cycle on the new furnace will save 30% on the utility bill in a oneyear period. This is an example of
explanation: A benefit. This is an advantage the customer receives from using a product. Customer feedback is informa-tion given by the customer to the salesperson. Showmanship is the use of dramatic techniques to show a product's features. A testimonial is a statement by an identified user of a product, as to the benefits s/he received from that product.

prompt: The salesperson should pause before answering a customer's objections in order to
choices: let the customer see that s/he is upset.
explanation: Get the customer's full attention. The salesperson should not rush to answer customers' objections, but s/he should not delay dealing with the objection. Instead, s/he should make sure the customer has finished, pause for a minute, collect his/her thoughts, and then respond calmly and quietly. This helps to show the customer that the salesperson is not upset about the objection. Showing empathy for customers involves letting them know that you understand their point of view.

prompt: The salesperson who is of the most benefit to the customer and to the business is the one who knows how to use
explanation: Suggestion selling. Suggestion selling benefits the business by building sales volume and profits. At the same time, it satisfies the customer to a greater degree by enabling him/her to make several purchases at one time and place. High-pressure tactics and too much talking produce negative results. Advertising attracts the customer to the business so that the salesperson can complete the selling job.

prompt: Determine whether the following statement is true or false: Follow-up should only be used when a sale has been completed.
choices: True, follow-up should be used after the approach.
False, follow-up should be used even if no sale is made.
True, follow-up should only be used when a sale is made.
False, follow-up should be used before the sale is completed.
explanation: False, follow-up should be used even if no sale is made. Good salespeople know that it is often wise to follow up with a customer who did not buy. The customer is usually pleased that the business would take time to find out whether it could be of any further service, and an eventual sale may result. The appropriate time to follow up when a sale has been made is shortly after the sale is completed. There are several steps in the selling process between the approach, the initial contact with the customer, and the follow-up.

prompt: Many businesses train employees to use sales tax charts to calculate sales tax on customers' purchases because the charts
choices: show the percent of tax due.
explanation: Make tax calculation easy. States provide businesses with tax charts, or schedules, that specify the correct percentage of sales tax to be charged in their states. These charts show exactly how much tax must be collected on the total amount of each sale. The charts help to reduce employee errors because they reduce the need for math. The employee must still add the correct amount of tax to the customer's total purchase or enter the amount into the cash register accurately.

prompt: A product's style, reorder, or catalog number is recorded in what part of the sales check?
explanation: Description. Products are identified on sales checks through style, reorder, or catalog number. In this way, the data can be used for inventory control, as well as a sales record. Terms on a sales check refer to the manner in which payment will be made. Quantity deals with the amount being sold, and department iden-tifies the area where the merchandise was purchased.

prompt: Salespeople who are prospecting can often obtain lists of current and past customers, credit records, and product inquiries from
explanation: Their own companies. Salespeople should remember that the companies for which they work can provide a wealth of information that will be useful in prospecting. Noncompeting salespeople, trade associations, and trade journals do not usually have access to information about others' current or past customers, their credit records, or product inquiries.

prompt: Many businesses try to increase sales by using sales quotas as a(n)
explanation: Challenge. Many salespeople consider sales quotas a challenge. Being able to achieve meaningful goals gives salespeople personal satisfaction and a sense of accomplishment. They often strive to outperform others and exceed quotas. Businesses may use quotas as the basis for punishing salespeople who do not perform. Making sales quotas a requirement or an obligation is not as likely to inspire salespeople who may consider the quotas a burden.
